before: ProGen3 is a sparse mixture-of-experts transformer. The 3B configuration has 24 layers, hidden size 1280, 16 attention heads, 8 experts with 2 chosen per token, SiLU-gated feed-forward blocks, RMS normalisation and rotary position embeddings. It is trained in both reading directions: a prompt starts with 1 for N-to-C or 2 for C-to-N, so the same model can extend a sequence from either end. A separate [GLM] prompt form asks the model to replace a named span of a given sequence with a chosen average number of residues, which is how infilling is done. Scoring averages the log-likelihood of the forward and reverse directions.
after: ProGen3 is a decoder-only transformer whose feed-forward layers are a mixture of 8 experts, 2 of which are used for each token, so a forward pass activates 27% of the parameters. The paper gives a context length of 8192 tokens, SwiGLU feed-forward networks, rotary position embeddings with theta 100000, grouped query attention and pre-layer RMS normalisation, with a load-balancing loss weighted 0.05. The released 3B configuration has 24 layers, hidden size 1280, 16 attention heads, intermediate size 3840 and a vocabulary of 134 tokens, matching the paper's table. It is trained in both reading directions: a prompt starts with 1 for N-to-C or 2 for C-to-N. A separate [GLM] prompt form asks the model to replace a named span of a given sequence, which is how infilling is done. Scoring averages the log-likelihood of the forward and reverse directions.
